title: Near DBL_MAX, ROUND returns NaN bit patterns that Excel treats as numbers
statement: ROUND of a number near 1.8E308 can return a binary64 with an all-ones exponent field: the decimal-to-binary conversion does not saturate, and a value of 1.8E308 comes out with the exponent overflowed. The bank holds 430 such ROUND rows, 102 ROUNDDOWN and 95 TRUNC. Even ROUND(DBL_MAX,0), whose answer is DBL_MAX, returns 0x7ff000000000000a. The cell shows 2E+308 or 1.8E+308, ISNUMBER gives TRUE, ISERROR FALSE, TYPE 1, and =A1, N(A1), MAX(A1), ABS(A1) and IFERROR(A1,...) pass the pattern on, as does =-A1 with its sign unchanged. Arithmetic on it (A1+0, A1*1, A1-A1, SUM, ROUND) gives #NUM!, TEXT(A1,"0") gives #VALUE!, ERROR.TYPE(A1) gives #N/A. Saved to .xlsx and reopened, the cells read #NUM! until recalculated, when the patterns return.
basis: One Excel workbook read cell by cell through Value2 on 2026-11-04, saved, reopened and recalculated; bank counts from the rounding write-up.
inferred: That one decimal-to-binary conversion routine is the source of all these patterns is inferred from the exponent-overflow encoding.

correct.how: DBL_MAX is an integer, so rounding it to 0 places returns it.
